claims.text: The baseline is an as-deposited, sputtered FeNiCrCoCu thin coating on a conventional metal substrate.
Post-deposition annealing will promote formation of Cu-rich nanoprecipitates in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The proposed annealing condition is approximately 700°C for 1–2 hours in an inert atmosphere.
The annealing treatment will enhance the formation and distribution of Cu-rich nanoprecipitates at grain boundaries.
The annealing treatment will enhance the formation and distribution of Cu-rich nanoprecipitates within the alloy matrix.
Cu-rich nanoprecipitates will act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
Cu-rich nanoprecipitates will distribute strain more uniformly during sliding.
Cu-rich nanoprecipitates will impede the initiation and propagation of localized shear deformation, including shear bands.
The precipitate-mediated inhibition of localized shear deformation will promote dynamic strain hardening.
The proposed precipitate-mediated mechanism will reduce the development of severe wear features during high-temperature sliding.
The annealed coating will have a lower macroscopic wear rate than the as-deposited coating.
The annealed coating will exhibit more homogeneous microscopic deformation than the as-deposited coating.
The annealed coating will exhibit fewer localized shear bands than the as-deposited coating.
The predicted effects are expected during sliding wear tests conducted at 600–700°C under controlled load and sliding speed.
The predicted wear and deformation improvements depend on the Cu-rich nanoprecipitates remaining stable during testing.
Coarsening or dissolution of Cu-rich nanoprecipitates during extended high-temperature exposure may diminish their effectiveness as dislocation barriers.
Loss of precipitate stability may diminish the predicted improvements in wear resistance and deformation behavior.
